caveats: Day LST of the 1990 and 1995 frames comes from Landsat 5 alone: some WRS-2 path/rows have fewer than 6 clear pre-monsoon scenes in the window, so these frames are tiered 'observed-sparse' and are noisier.
The 2005 day frame includes Landsat 7 ETM+ scenes after the 2003 scan-line-corrector failure (SLC-off): striped gaps are filled only by other scenes of the window.

Day LST is a ~10:30 IST snapshot; frames are corrected to a common 10:45 IST overpass with an ERA5-Land skin-temperature heating rate. The correction (typically a few tenths of a degree, more for early Landsat 5 scenes) carries its own uncertainty, included in the level intervals.

Night LST is in Aqua-equivalent units: the 2025 frame is VIIRS and the 2000 frame Terra (22:30), both calibrated to Aqua on overlap years; 1990 and 1995 night frames are model hindcasts, not observations.
ERA5-Land climate covariates have ~9-11 km native resolution (bilinearly resampled to the grid) and known warm/dry biases over irrigated Indo-Gangetic cropland.
Land cover is GLC_FCS30D for every frame (five-yearly maps before 2000, ~81 % global accuracy); the 2025 frame uses its 2022 map.
GHSL built-up and population for 2025 and 2030 are model extrapolations (GHSL P2023A), and GHSL accuracy before 2000 is lower (Landsat back-casting).

Projections 2030-2050 are scenario projections, not forecasts: they combine CMIP6 temperature deltas scaled by an empirical dLST/dTair sensitivity with simulated land change, with Monte-Carlo uncertainty.
SHAP values explain the model's predictions, not causal effects; thresholds and recommendations are model-based what-if estimates.
PILOT RUN: only the 1990, 2000, 2020, 2025 frames and no projections (Earth Engine cost probe); not a complete analysis.
Day frame 1990 (1989-1992): fewer than 6 clear Landsat scenes on path/row(s) 146/040 (3), 146/041 (3) - tiered observed-sparse.
Landsat day frame 1990: large path 146-147 offset +4.25 °C (different dates or weather on the two paths) - removed symmetrically.
MODIS Terra day LST of the 2025 frame comes from drifted orbits (~10:07 IST in 2025); after the 10.0-11.5 h view-time filter 100 % of the ROI keeps a value. It is a validation layer only.
MODIS Terra day annual means are missing where fewer than 50 % of the cells keep a value after the QC and 10.0-11.5 h view-time filters (years [2025]).

Night LST of the 2025 frame is VIIRS S-NPP (TES algorithm) and of the 2000 frame MODIS Terra (22:30 IST); both are mapped to Aqua (split-window, ~02:12 IST) by per-class overlap calibrations whose leave-one-year-out errors are reported in metrics.night_calibration.
GHSL built-up, volume and population of the 2025 frame are GHSL P2023A extrapolations.
Land cover of the 2025 frame (and of any frame after 2022) is the GLC_FCS30D 2022 map.
SSP population growth is the IIASA SSP v3 national urban-population trajectory of India (no NCR-specific SSP projection exists in the SSP database); it scales the NCR population total.
Chen et al. (2020) SSP urban land is binary at 1 km; it enters only as district growth ratios relative to its own 2020 layer.

The night fixed mask (cells with a valid target in every training frame with >= 50% coverage) keeps only 76.9% of the ROI cells; missing share of the ROI per frame: 2020 23.1%, 2025 0.0%. Frame levels and anomalies refer to this cell set.
